topic: What happens when you crack your knuckles?
title: What Happens When You Crack Your Knuckles?
sources: Kawchuk GN, Fryer J, Jaremko JL, Zeng H, Rowe L, Thompson R. 'Real-Time Visualization of Joint Cavitation.' PLoS ONE 2015;10(4):e0119470 (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0119470): real-time cine MRI showed the cracking sound coincides with rapid cavity INCEPTION in synovial fluid (tribonucleation), NOT collapse of a pre-existing bubble; the event lasts under 310 ms; the refractory period before a joint can crack again is about 20 minutes (Roston & Wheeler Haines 1947)

deWeber K, Olszewski M, Ortolano R. 'Knuckle cracking and hand osteoarthritis.' J Am Board Fam Med 2011;24(2):169-74 (PMID 21383216): in 215 people, no correlation between habitual knuckle cracking and hand osteoarthritis

Powers T, Kelsberg G, Safranek S. 'Clinical Inquiry: Does knuckle popping lead to arthritis?' J Fam Pract 2016;65(10):725-726 (PMID 27846331): habitual knuckle cracking over several decades is not associated with clinical or radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis

lines.text: What actually happens when you crack your knuckles?
Stretch the joint, and the fluid inside instantly forms a gas cavity.
In 2015, scientists caught it live on an MRI.
lines.caps: In *2015 | scientists | caught it *live | on an *MRI

lines.text: The pop is the bubble being born, not bursting.
That's why you can't crack the same knuckle for about twenty minutes.
lines.caps: That's why | you *can't | crack it *again | for *20 minutes

lines.text: So does it wreck your joints?
Researchers followed habitual crackers for years.
The sound is physics, not damage.
Now you can un-hear the myth.
